summary: GLP-1 radar for Oct 12, 2026. Every topic here sits inside the GLP-1 focus. The plague topics from earlier snapshots are left out because the brief limits topics to GLP-1. Their momentum is also slowly dropping (86 → 80). I checked the top candidates with web searches. I estimated YouTube and TikTok competition from news density and did not count videos directly. Best openings: (1) Nail detachment on GLP-1s. An EADV 2026 survey reports 39% vs 9% (not peer reviewed). It is just reaching ScienceDaily, so it is early and the search question is plain. It needs a calm, hedged, 'don't stop on your own' angle. (2) Weight regain after stopping. A pilot RCT (n=39) found about 10.75% regain with usual care vs about 3.6% with an app or medically tailored meals. It reached News-Medical, Newsweek and Epocrates in 5 days. (3) Semaglutide for heavy drinking. A Lancet RCT (n=108) found 13.7 percentage points fewer heavy-drinking days. It is moving from medical outlets toward the mainstream. (4) Retatrutide explainer. Search demand is very high (WCNC VERIFY, Women's Health, Washington Post, Medscape gray-market story). Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027, so it is not approved. Competition is high, but our proven named-drug decoder format fits. We must frame it as 'not approved, gray-market products are a risk'. (5) The Wegovy pill takes off. JAMA Netw Open counted 148,792 starts in about 12 weeks. Other good options: liver fat (STEP UP post hoc plus new EASL-EASD-EASO MASH guidance), smell and taste changes (0.37% vs 0.22%), biological aging (hype check), GLP-1 side effects vs lawsuits (NPR), Zepbound plus Taltz in psoriasis, frailty and falls, and an EloraTZP follow-up (our best long-form subject so far). Rejected: compounded telehealth price ads ($86/month) and any retatrutide 'where to buy' or microdosing content. Per the playbook, Short titles should use a recognizable drug or subject plus one plain number. Named-drug trial decoders should be the long-forms. Carousels are left out because none has reached more than 2 accounts.

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and nail problems: EADV 2026 survey reports nail detachment in 39% of GLP-1 users vs 9% of controls (not yet peer reviewed)
candidates.angle: 'Your nails on a GLP-1: what a new study found.' Give the numbers with hedges: a survey of about 1,900 people, self-reported, presented as an abstract, not peer reviewed. Researchers say rapid weight loss and eating less may explain it rather than the drug itself. Practical, positive steps: get enough protein, eat a balanced diet, mention nail changes to your prescriber, and don't stop treatment on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (ScienceDaily pickup on Oct 12; consumer outlets and TikTok usually follow within a week)
candidates.why_now: First controlled data on GLP-1 and nail changes. Presented at EADV 2026, covered by HCPLive and Medical Economics (Oct 1) and Advisory Board (Oct 6), and now on ScienceDaily (Oct 12). Mainstream coverage hasn't arrived yet. 'Ozempic nails' is a plain, visual search question.

evidence.signal: Nail detachment 4 times more common with GLP-1 use. EADV 2026, not peer reviewed
GLP-1 users report more nail detachment and hair loss than non-users
Pickup in health-system news
Popular weight loss drugs linked to a surprising fingernail problem

candidates.topic: Weight regain after stopping a GLP-1: pilot RCT finds about 10.75% regain with usual care vs about 3.6% with a coaching app or medically tailored meals over 4 months
candidates.angle: 'Stopping a GLP-1: what slowed weight regain in a new trial.' Hopeful and practical. Structured support (meals or a digital program) was linked to less early regain. Caveats: a small pilot (n=39), 4 months only, and adherence and satisfaction didn't differ between groups. Stopping is a decision to make with your prescriber. Pair it with the bigger picture (SURMOUNT-4 regain data). Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
keywords: how to keep weight off after GLP-1
candidates.predicted_peak: 5–14 days (evergreen demand plus a fresh RCT hook)
candidates.why_now: Published in Obes Sci Pract on Oct 7 and picked up by News-Medical, Newsweek, Epocrates and health-system blogs within 5 days. Employee Benefit News is also running 'beware of cutting off GLP-1s too soon'. Keeping results after stopping is one of the top questions our audience asks.

evidence.signal: Pilot RCT, 39 adults: usual care vs Noom vs medically tailored meals after GLP-1 stop

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and alcohol: Lancet RCT (n=108, adults with alcohol use disorder and obesity) found 13.7 percentage points fewer heavy-drinking days vs placebo over 26 weeks
candidates.angle: 'Semaglutide and alcohol: what a new Lancet trial found.' Tie it to the brain's reward system and 'food noise'. Exact population: moderate-to-severe AUD plus obesity, with CBT in both arms. Craving and liver markers improved. It is not approved for alcohol use disorder. Anyone worried about their drinking should talk to a clinician. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Lancet publication covered by EMJ, PsyPost and Medical Economics (Oct 11 Morning Medical Update). 'Ozempic and alcohol cravings' is already a common question among users, and this is RCT-level evidence.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide cuts heavy drinking in AUD trial (Lancet, 26 weeks, 2.4 mg vs placebo)

candidates.topic: What is retatrutide ('reta')? The triple-hormone drug explained: Phase 3 results, not FDA approved, Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027, and why gray-market 'reta' is a risk
candidates.angle: Named-drug decoder (our best long-form format): 'Retatrutide: what the trials show and when it could arrive.' Explain how it works on GLP-1, GIP and glucagon, what the trials found, and the status. Lilly has sued sellers of unapproved products, and Medscape reported a gray-market harm case. Never name or link sources. Say clearly: no approved product exists, so wait and talk to your doctor about approved options. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.predicted_peak: Now through 2 weeks (long tail until the 2027 filing)
candidates.why_now: Many sources at once: WCNC 'VERIFY: What is RETA?' (Oct 12), Washington Post (Oct 10), two Women's Health pieces, Medscape 'Gray-Market Retatrutide' (Oct 9), TCTMD on diabetes data, and Pharma Voice on Lilly fighting a black market. Search-style headlines show strong question demand.

candidates.topic: The Wegovy pill takes off: JAMA Netw Open counts 148,792 US adults starting oral semaglutide in about 12 weeks, and more than half had never used a GLP-1
candidates.angle: 'Wegovy pill vs the shot: who's choosing it and what to ask.' Show who is starting it (older, more often women, more Medicare coverage) and why a pill matters for people who avoid needles. Compare the pill and the injection using trial data, without dosing. Tirzepatide is still the most-started medicine. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: JAMA Netw Open study (Oct 1) covered by Physician's Weekly and Epocrates. Yahoo ran 'Wegovy pill or Wegovy shot?' (Oct 10), The Pharma Letter covered it (Oct 12), and the Times ran 'New Wegovy jab'. Searches like 'how effective is the wegovy pill' are appearing.

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and fatty liver: STEP UP post hoc found liver fat fell below 5% in 23 of 26 adults with obesity (EASD 2026), plus new EASL-EASD-EASO guidance on semaglutide and resmetirom for MASH
candidates.angle: 'Fatty liver on a GLP-1: what new data and new guidelines say.' Explain MASLD and MASH simply. Give 23 of 26 with its caveats: small subgroup, post hoc, no placebo comparison reported. Then explain what the new European guidance means. This fits our benefits-beyond-weight pillar. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: Pharmacy Times (Oct 6–10) and the Novo release covered the liver-fat result. EASL-EASD-EASO guidance was reported Oct 12. Fatty liver is a big, under-served search topic among our audience.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide normalized liver fat in most adults with obesity (23 of 26, MRI-PDFF, post hoc)

candidates.topic: EloraTZP follow-up: 23.3% vs 14.8% weight loss over 48 weeks in people with diabetes, but more people stopped because of side effects (11–27%)
candidates.angle: Follow up our best long-form ever (216 views). 'EloraTZP side effects: why more people stopped.' Show both sides: bigger weight loss, but more stopped because of side effects. Explain how amylin plus GLP-1/GIP works. It is investigational, not approved. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: The Motley Fool and AOL ran pieces Oct 12 on the 'combination for Eli Lilly' with higher discontinuation, after STAT's Sep 30 report. Our audience already responded to this drug name.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 side effects: what's actually known vs what lawsuits claim (NPR Oct 7; J Intern Med review of serious adverse events, Oct 9)
candidates.angle: Calm, balanced decoder: 'GLP-1 side effects: common vs rare, and what we still don't know.' Common: nausea, constipation and other GI effects, which get easier with practical habits. Rare and debated: which events are supported by evidence and which are uncertain. A lawsuit is an allegation, not proof. Know the warning signs and when to call your prescriber. Never use fear framing. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: NPR syndicated the story to affiliates Oct 7–10. The J Intern Med review (Oct 9) offers a peer-reviewed counterweight. Lawsuit stories on vision loss (Sept) are still circulating.

evidence.signal: Some who take GLP-1s are suffering serious side effects, but it's unclear how often

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and smell or taste changes: 0.37% vs 0.22% diagnosed over 2 years (JAMA Otolaryngology, about 438,000 matched adults with type 2 diabetes)
candidates.angle: 'Food tastes different on Ozempic? What a big study found.' Relative risk sounds big (48% higher), but the absolute numbers are small (0.37% vs 0.22%). Tie it to GLP-1 receptors in sensory pathways as a hypothesis. Mention it to your prescriber if it happens. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.

candidates.topic: Can GLP-1s slow biological aging? Semaglutide was linked to about 9% slower epigenetic aging vs placebo in a 32-week trial in adults with HIV-associated lipohypertrophy
candidates.angle: Hype check: 'Ozempic and aging: what the study really measured.' Explain DNA-methylation clocks, the specific population, and that a 32-week result can't show longer life. It may work through less visceral fat and inflammation. There is no evidence healthy people should take it for longevity. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
candidates.why_now: NewsNation (Oct 12) is reviving 'GLP-1s slow biological aging' after the summer study. Longevity framing spreads fast on TikTok, and a calm correction is needed.

Exact population: moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis plus obesity or overweight with a comorbidity. The biomarker data is exploratory. Talk to your doctor or prescriber.
